previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following his third transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure targeting residual tumors in liver segments VI, VII, and VIII. The procedure was successfully performed via the right femoral artery, delivering doxorubicin-eluting beads to the tumor sites. A previously suspected phrenic artery supply was not identified, but a feeding vessel from the right adrenal/intercostal artery was successfully coiled and embolized to prevent non-target perfusion. The patient tolerated the procedure well, with no immediate complications, pain, or bleeding at the access site. He remained stable throughout the admission, with mild expected changes in liver enzymes. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor for post-embolization syndrome, continue all home medications, and follow up with oncology and hepatology in four weeks for imaging and treatment reassessment.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man with multifocal HCC s/p TACE. // RFA to residual
tumor and 2 additional sites.

OPERATORS:  Dr ___ imaging fellow) and Dr ___
radiologist) performed the procedure. The attending radiologist was present
and supervising throughout the entirety of the procedure.

DOSE:  676 mGy-cm

FINDINGS: 

Limited preprocedure CT scan of the abdomen was performed for purposes of RFA
planning. This demonstrated a sidewall in the abdomen segment 7 lesion. The
portion enhancing on prior MRI to not contain a sidewall, which were targeted
for RFA ablation. The additional 2 segment 8 lesions to be targeted are not
well visualized on noncontrast examination.

Findings of cirrhosis liver with splenomegaly and collateral vessels. Right
renal cysts. Gallstones.

Arterial imaging of the abdomen was later performed after administration of
100cc of IV contrast material after the first ablation was completed.

COMPARISON:  Abdomen from ___ and chemoembolization from ___.

SEDATION:  General anesthesia was administered by the anesthesiologist
department. Please see their notes for dedicated details.

PROCEDURE:  Radiofrequency ablation of the segment 7 residual lesion.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient and informed written consent was obtained. An
approach to ablation was determined with the patient in a supine position and
the access site was marked with ink on the patient's skin surface. A
pre-procedure timeout was then performed using three patient identifiers was
performed per ___ protocol.

The access site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. A 20 cm
length cluster radiofrequency ablation probe was advanced into the liver to
the targeted segment 7 lesion, its medial and inferior portion under CT
guidance. Confirmation of its position was performed under CT fluoroscopy.
Radiofrequency ablation was then performed for a total of 12 min with maximal
temperature of 88 degrees Celsius. During the ablation of this lesion, the
ablation was halted 2 times for hypertension due to irritation of the
immediately adjacent adrenal gland. Blood pressure was monitored and
controlled by the anesthesia team. Once blood pressure was in an acceptable
range, the ablation continued for a total of 12 min.

The cluster probe was then slowly withdrawn and readjusted into the superior
portion of the medial aspect of the lesion and ablation was then performed for
an additional 10 min with maximal temperature of 88 degrees Celsius. The
ablation probe was then removed, with low energy ablation of the tract
performed along the way. A limited, arterial CT of the abdomen was then
performed after administration of 100 mL of IV contrast material to locate the
additional 2 segment 8 lesions and to assess the ablation coverage of the
segment 7 lesion as the segment 8 lesions are not visible under ultrasound. At
this time, it was noted that there was new free fluid surrounding the liver
and to a lesser extent along the inferior spleen and right paracolic gutter.
There is high-density material along the ablation tract extending into the
subcapsular region, compatible with hemorrhage. The patient's blood pressure
was slightly hypotensive at this time, which was managed by the anesthesia
department. It is unclear whether the slightly low blood pressures were due to
the hemorrhage or due to the control of the recent hypertension. The decision
was made to terminate the procedure at this time and take the patient to the
angiography suite for embolization of the bleed. The patient left the
department in stable condition.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Successful radiofrequency ablation of the residual segment 7 tumor.

2. The patient became hypertensive during the ablation of the segment 7 tumor
due to its immediate proximity to the adrenal gland, which was controlled by
the anesthesiology department.

3. At the conclusion of the segment 7 ablation after the probe was removed,
limited imaging through the area demonstrated arterial extravasation from the
ablation tract. The decision was made to terminate the procedure without
ablating the additional two segment 8 lesions and instead go to the
angiography suite for embolization.

4. Please see dedicated dictation for full details on the embolization
procedure.

INDICATION:  ___ MALE WITH ACTIVE BLEEDING ON POST RFA CT.  HEPATIC
ARTERY ANGIOGRAM AND EMBOLIZATION REQUESTED.

COMPARISON:  Same day CT abdomen and chemoembolization of the liver ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ (interventional radiology fellow) and
Dr. ___ (interventional radiology attending) performed the procedure.
The attending was present and supervising throughout the procedure.

ANESTHESIA: General anesthesia was provided for the duration today's case.  1%
lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the
access site

CONTRAST: 125 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 29.5 min, 1168 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Right common femoral artery access.

2. Common hepatic digital subtraction arteriogram and 3D CT

3. Digital subtraction angiogram of right middle adrenal artery.

4. Right common femoral artery closed using Angio Seal device.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient's wife as
the patient was already under general anesthesia for the ___ procedure.. The
patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol. The
right groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Using palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral artery was
punctured using a micropuncture set at the level of the mid-femoral head. A
0.018 wire was passed easily into the vessel lumen. A small skin incision was
made over the needle. Then the inner dilator and wire were removed and a
___ wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta. The micropuncture
sheath was exchanged for a 5 ___ sheath which was attached to a continuous
heparinized saline side arm flush.

A C2 Cobra glide catheter was advanced over ___ wire into the aorta. The
wire was removed and the celiac artery was selectively cannulated and a small
contrast injection was made to confirm position. A glidewire was then advanced
into the common hepatic artery and a Glide catheter advanced to the common
hepatic artery. A digital subtraction angiogram and 3D spin CT was performed.

3D CT was performed under the direct supervision of the attending supervision.
Reformatted images were obtained using a separate workstation. The information
gained from these reformatted images were crucial in the success of the case.

At this time the Cobra catheter was removed and ___ catheter advanced
over the ___ wire and formed in the aorta. The ___ catheter was used
to select out the right renal artery which had a common trunk of the right
middle adrenal artery and right phrenic artery. Digital subtraction angiogram
was performed. A combination of micro catheters and micro wires were used in
an attempt to further select out the adrenal and phrenic arteries, however,
all were unsuccessful.

The catheter was then removed over the wire and the sheath was removed.
Angioseal device was used to achieve hemostasis of the right common femoral
artery puncture site. Sterile dressings were applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  No immediate complications. Patient
transferred to the PACU.

FINDINGS: 

1. DSA and 3D CT of the common hepatic artery demonstrated no evidence of
active extravasation.

2. DSA of right renal artery ostium containing take-offs of the right middle
adrenal artery and right phrenic artery demonstrate no evidence of active
extravasation.

3. Angio Seal device placed for closure.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of active extravasation demonstrated during today's procedure.
